article_title: Career regret, academic-related factors and health-related quality of life among Syrian medical students: a multicentre cross-sectional study.
citation: Kheder Maria, Nasra Ahmad Bishr, Alghoutani Sarah, Al-Hammash Hiba, Saleh Abdullah, Assaad Alaa, Almansour Shahd, Kreimesh Nussaiba, Kanaa Leen, Latifeh Youssef, Alsaid Bayan. (2026). Career regret, academic-related factors and health-related quality of life among Syrian medical students: a multicentre cross-sectional study. BMJ Open. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2026-118578
title: Regret-5 Mean (R5M), a study-developed five-item career-regret measure for medical students
description: The R5M is a composite score calculated as the mean of five Likert-rated statements about choosing medicine again, recommending medicine, considering medicine an ideal career, disappointment with medical school and thoughts of leaving, with higher scores indicating greater regret. The article reports the measure showed "good internal consistency (Cronbach's α=0.831)" and a one-factor structure (loadings 0.608–0.834) in this sample. It served as the continuous primary outcome in bivariate and regression analyses.
requirements: Items reverse-scored so higher values consistently indicate greater regret; all items share the same five-point response range for equal weighting
constraints: The measure had not undergone external validation or a structured content-validity assessment
The exploratory R5M≥2.5 subgroup threshold is not a validated diagnostic or clinical cut-off
target_learners: medical students in academic years two through six
target_learning_goals: measuring career regret and attitudes toward the medical career choice
examples: Administered in Arabic and English to 1,702 students across public and private Syrian universities between May and July 2025
